_comment: pi-lean-ctx configuration. `enableMcp` is true because it is a correctness setting, not a performance one — it decides which of lean-ctx's two caches serves ctx_read. lean-ctx deliberately collapses a repeat `read -m full` of an unchanged file to a ~13-token stub; its own help documents this (`full — Full content (cached re-reads = 13 tokens)`) and `lean-ctx verify-cache` proves it. The design assumes the caller still holds the content from the first read. That holds inside one session and fails across sessions — and with enableMcp false, ctx_read uses the CLI cache, which is disk-backed, cross-process and user-scoped. A fresh session, a subagent, or a read after compaction then receives the stub for content it has never seen, while the footer still reports `Compressed N -> 13 tokens (-99%)`, which is indistinguishable from a genuine compression win. The MCP bridge's cache is per-session, so the assumption holds and the stub only ever replaces content the session already has. Verified 2026-08-15 with binary 3.9.13: a fresh session read a file that was already stubbed in the CLI cache and received full content. The bridge spawns the `lean-ctx` binary at session start, and that binary is not a dependency of this repository — install it with `cargo install lean-ctx --version 3.9.13` (3.9.14 through 3.9.18 failed to build when measured on 2026-08-15: they require `lean-ctx-ocla ^1.0.0` and the only version of that crate published at the time lacked fields the code references. `lean-ctx-ocla 1.0.1` was published on 2026-08-26 and `lean-ctx 3.9.20` pins it, so that cause has expired; nothing has been rebuilt to confirm, and 3.9.13 stays the pinned install). With no binary on PATH the bridge costs a failed spawn plus backoff retries and several stderr lines per startup; if you do not want the binary, remove the package rather than setting this to false, because false is only safe for as long as the binary stays absent.
